description:
A substrate-authored commit made llm-resolver-vessel crash on boot whenever ANY wired provider has an empty API key, taking down the entire LLM plane and with it every compose in the fleet. Edit repos/llm-resolver-vessel/src/index.ts.
OPERATOR WORKAROUND CURRENTLY IN PLACE - READ BEFORE TOUCHING CREDENTIALS. To clear the fleet-wide outage, /etc/substrate/env now sets five provider keys to the literal string "unset-placeholder": GOOGLE_API_KEY, GROQ_API_KEY, MISTRAL_API_KEY, RUNPOD_API_KEY, VLLM_API_KEY. A backup of the original file is at /etc/substrate/env.bak-preplaceholder.
THESE ARE SENTINELS, NOT CREDENTIALS. Their only purpose is to be non-empty so `new OpenAI({ apiKey })` constructs instead of throwing at module scope. Calls through those providers will fail per-request, which is the intended fail-fast behaviour f4bae3c described.
CONSEQUENCES TO HANDLE WHEN FIXING THIS PROPERLY: (1) once the code substitutes its own sentinel for an empty key, these env entries should be returned to empty or to real keys - leaving a fake key set is indistinguishable from a real one to any future reader; (2) anyone funding real credentials must OVERWRITE these, not assume the provider is unconfigured, because the vessel will now report the arm as present-but-failing rather than dark; (3) do not treat "unset-placeholder" appearing in a quota or health report as evidence of a configured provider.
